findings.quote: That gap was put to a working bay.
findings.note: class 3: 'put to X' is idiomatic only with test/use/sword etc.; 'put to a working bay' compresses out 'the test' and lands as a strained collocation an editor would query; editor's rewrite: 'That gap was put to the test at a working bay.'

findings.quote: That gap was put to a working bay.
findings.note: class 3: collocation miss; "put to X" idiomatically completes as put to the test/to a vote/to use, not put to a place; the elliptical compression parses awkwardly even in a terse columnist voice; editor's rewrite: 'That gap was put to the test in a working bay.'

findings.quote: They laid down more nacre, and would have gone on adding thickness without any limit at all, however long the oysters were simply left completely alone.
findings.note: B is an unbounded absolute; D changes the measured quantity from amount of nacre to its colour and lustre, off the stem's axis. Two eliminate on form, leaving A (dose-response) vs C (flat margin) genuinely open without the passage.

findings.quote: Because only constant handling can make a pearl round, and any oyster left in peace for long is bound to build a worthless, lumpy coat.
findings.note: B falls as an 'only ... bound to' absolute and C is self-undermining as stated ('a thinner coat is naturally rounder'), so two go on form. A remains a substantive confound (cooler, cleaner water), so A vs D still requires the passage.

ARGUABLE: "The old assumption that a voice was the warmest way to reach another person has, Vinderhed suggests, quietly ___(5)___" accepts 'collapsed' — 'quietly collapsed' is idiomatic for a failure that happened without fanfare, and "how quickly the etiquette has hardened" supports a sudden reading. Beatable: the passage's evidence is a decade-long drift ('across a decade the share ... has roughly halved'), and 'lapse' is the precise verb for a belief or practice falling out of force by degrees. Pre-existing and rename-independent — the entity repair touched only names in the passage.

findings.quote: To make each guest's card stop working once they left, so a copied or unreturned credential could no longer open the room
findings.note: World knowledge of recodable keycard-lock history (the security/expiring-credential motive, cf. VingCard 1975-76) points to B; A is the 'obvious convenience' answer the framing rejects. C/D are substantive aims, so key not decided by form alone (WORLD_KNOWLEDGE).

findings.quote: The grit and salt that traffic drags over the line, together with snowplough blades, rather than its age or tyres running over it
findings.note: A is the comprehensive option that names and rebuts B (tyres) and C (age) directly; combined with general knowledge of road-marking abrasion this leans A without the passage (WORLD/partial).

findings.quote: en självförsörjande gård förväntades dra sitt eget
findings.note: class 6: 'dra sitt eget' reads as an elided 'dra sitt (eget) lass'; standing alone the object-less idiom is unidiomatic/incomplete. native alternative: 'dra sitt eget lass' or 'klara sig själv'

findings.quote: Så snart det fanns en bryggare i orten överlevde humlegårdarna längre, oberoende av hur marken låg.
findings.note: C is an 'oberoende av' absolute and D presents the source work (drygt tolvtusen jämförbara noteringar) as the main finding; both fall on form. A and B are the same association with the arrow reversed, and the direction is not decidable without the passage.

findings.quote: Landskapslagarna krävde sedan medeltiden att varje hemman höll en humlegård med bestämt antal stänger, annars hotade böter.
findings.note: Answerable from domain knowledge rather than from form: the Swedish humleodlingstvang - the medieval provincial-law and landslag requirement that each hemman keep a hop garden of a set number of stanger on pain of a fine - is a real, documented statute, so a solver who knows Swedish agrarian legal history picks C without the text. Routed to adjudication rather than killed because the three foils (crown plantations, hops as a church tithe, a protectionist origin after cheap imports) are substantively plausible institutional alternatives, not filler, and no form asymmetry separates them; the orchestrator may still wish to treat this as recall-only.

findings.quote: På åsjorden kunde humlen aldrig drabbas av rötskador, och därför behövde en gård där aldrig överges.
findings.note: D is a double 'aldrig' absolute and B contradicts the stem's own presupposition (the stem asks why the gardens on the dry ridge soil did best, while B denies that the soil mattered); both go on form. A is additionally favoured because it simply unpacks the stem's own word 'torra' into a drainage mechanism, but C offers a substantive competing property of ridge soil, so the item is not fully decided blind.

class 6: 'blöta ner' is transitive (regnet blöter ner marken); with 'marken' as an intransitive subject it is off-valence — the ground gets wet, it does not itself 'wet down'. native alternative: 'när marken blir blöt' / 'när underlaget blöts upp'

findings.quote: De värst uttrampade partierna låg oftast där leden korsade blöt mark, inte där flest gick
findings.note: Counterintuitive-finding construction: B is the naive expectation and C its internal inversion, both eliminable by form, leaving A vs D as the non-naive alternatives (PARTIALLY).

findings.quote: Slitaget beror mer på markens väta än på antalet vandrare, vilket gör spänger verksammare än förbud
findings.note: B is an overreach absolute ('alla besöksförbud... verkningslösa'), A a false detail (slope), D a minor caveat, leaving C as the qualified main-message option. Form-level narrowing (PARTIALLY).

findings.quote: Efterfrågan på kontanter försvann inte utan samlades hos ett fåtal handlare med växande börda
findings.note: C is an absolute ('upphörde helt'), A reverses the stem's causal direction, D misstates the survey's scope, leaving B as the lean. Narrows without the passage (PARTIALLY).

findings.quote: Rätten att betala kontant bör tryggas som en gemensam angelägenhet, inte lämnas åt marknaden ensam
findings.note: Op-ed stance spectrum: C and D are extremes and B a position the piece disclaims, leaving A as the measured thesis. Genre/construction lean without the passage (PARTIALLY).
